body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\rm adap}\), construct one \(a\)-independent sample-split convex-projection test with rejection probability at most \(\alpha+o(1)\) uniformly over \(\{P\in\mathcal P_K^{\cup}:d(P)=0\}\), and with power at \(\Lambda_{\rm adap}(n,K)r_{n,K}(a,\beta)\), where \(\Lambda_{\rm adap}(n,K)\) is the smallest attainable adaptation factor. The calibration must resample training and testing uncertainty and remain valid on all source and box faces. Invert the resulting family of sublevel-set tests to obtain a lower confidence bound for \(d(P)\) with frontier-order stochastic width.
body.justification: Sharp rates are operational only with a calibration that survives nonregular active faces and unknown proxy strength.
body.gap: Fang and Seo require a fixed cone, while Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos do not analyze a growing image transported by a separately estimated operator.
body.consumer: Wu et al.'s binary-event discrete workflow receives a level-certified rejection rule and a quantitative lower bound on observable misspecification.

obligation.what_is_open: The smallest adaptation factor and a frontier-order joint multiplier calibration over all moving source and box faces remain unproved.
obligation.obstruction: The oracle frontier required to define the sharp factor is unresolved, and the projection map is directionally nonregular at active faces. Resampling only the testing fold would omit the training contribution established in the finite-sample decomposition.
obligation.attempted: The conservative split projection rule was calibrated by a simultaneous finite-sample event, yielding exact union-null level and an honest lower confidence bound. This does not provide the requested sharp multiplier law or prove minimality of an adaptation penalty.
obligation.partial_result:
The existing rule \(\phi_{\rm sp}\) is independent of \(a\) and has finite-sample level at most \(\alpha\) over the complete union null, with both folds and every active face covered deterministically by the projection comparison.  It has power at separation \(t_\alpha+t_\zeta\).  Moreover, on \(|\widehat d_{\rm sp}-d(P)|\le t_\alpha\),
\[
 0\le d(P)-L_n\le2t_\alpha,
\]
so \(L_n\) is an honest adaptive lower confidence bound with conservative width \(2t_\alpha\).  No comparison of this width with the unresolved sharp frontier, and hence no smallest \(\Lambda_{\rm adap}(n,K)\), is currently proved.
